{{Short description|Russian-American theoretical physicist}}
'''Arkady Vainshtein''' ({{langx|ru|Аркáдий Иóсифович Вайнштéйн}}; born 24 February 1942) is a Russian and American Professor Emeritus of [[Theoretical physics]] who was awarded [[Pomeranchuk Prize]] (2005) and [[Sakurai Prize]] (1999) for theoretical physics.<ref name=physics>{{cite web|url=http://www.physics.umn.edu/people/vainshte.html|title=Arkady Vainshtein UMN Physics BIO|accessdate=28 July 2019}}</ref>

==Biography==
Vainshtein was born on 24 February 1942 in [[Novokuznetsk]], Russia. He got his Ph.D. from [[Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics]] in [[Novosibirsk]], Russia and master's degree from [[Novosibirsk University]]<ref>[http://gold.vixpo.nsu.ru/default.aspx?db=museum_1959&int=VIEW&el=4316&templ=FOND_VIEW About Vainshtein in Russian] Retrieved 28 July 2019.</ref> where he became a Professor. He was the director of [[William I Fine Theoretical Physics Institute, University of Minnesota]] where he currently serves as the Gloria Becker Lubkin chair<ref name=physics/> and also holds a position as Professor since 1990. In 1997 he became a fellow at the [[American Physical Society|APS]]<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1997&unit_id=&institution=University+of+Minnesota}} (search on year=1997 and institution=University of Minnesota)</ref> and two years later was awarded [[Sakurai Prize]]. In 2004 he started to work for [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]] in [[Santa Barbara, California|Santa Barbara]], [[California]], and a year later was awarded [[Pomeranchuk Prize]] from the [[Institute for Theoretical and Experimental Physics]], [[Moscow]].<ref name=physics/> Professor Vainshtein was awarded the 2014 Julius Wess Award by The KIT Center Elementary Particle and Astroparticle Physics (KCETA)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kceta.kit.edu/english/julius-wess-preis-2014.php|title=Julius Wess Award|accessdate=28 July 2019|date=2018-04-30}}</ref> and the 2016 [[Dirac Medal of the ICTP]].<ref>[https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/prizes-awards/the-dirac-medal/the-medallists/dirac-medallists-2016.aspx Dirac Medallists 2016] Retrieved 28 July 2019.</ref>
